en: Oṃ, salutations to the illustrious Hari and the Guru. Hariḥ Oṃ.

Of this *Śrī Pañcamukhī Vīra Hanumat Kavaca Stotra Mantra*: Brahmā is the seer (*ṛṣi*); Gāyatrī is the meter (*chanda*); the Supreme Self in the form of Śrī Rāmacandra, who possesses five faces, is the deity (*devatā*); *rhāṃ* is the seed-syllable (*bīja*); *rhīṃ* is the power (*śakti*); and "Candra" (the Moon) is the pin (*kīlaka*). The application (*viniyoga*) is for the sake of attaining grace through the recitation of the Supreme Self in the form of Śrī Rāmacandra, who resides within the five faces.
Now follows the ritual assignment of the fingers (aṅgulī-nyāsa).

Oṃ rhāṃ, salutation to the two thumbs. Oṃ rhīṃ, salutation to the two index fingers. Oṃ rhūṃ, salutation to the two middle fingers. Oṃ rhaiṃ, salutation to the two ring fingers. Oṃ rhauṃ, salutation to the two little fingers. Oṃ rhaḥ, salutation to the palms and backs of the hands. Thus is the ritual placement on the hands (karanyāsa).
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the heart and other limbs.

Oṃ rhāṃ, salutation to the heart. Oṃ rhīṃ, svāhā to the head. Oṃ rhūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the tuft of hair. Oṃ rhaiṃ, huṃ to the armor. Oṃ rhauṃ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes. Oṃ rhaḥ, phaṭ to the weapon. Thus is the placement of the heart (hṛdayanyāsa). Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ om.
Now, the binding of the directions.

Oṃ kaṃ khaṃ ghaṃ gaṃ ṅaṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ paṃ phaṃ baṃ bhaṃ maṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ haṃ laṃ kṣaṃ svāhā. Thus is the binding of the directions (digbandha).
Now, meditation.

I bow to Him who possesses the faces of a monkey, a man-lion, the king of birds, a boar, a bull, and a horse; who is adorned with divine ornaments, has fifteen eyes, and blazes brilliantly with Vedic hymns.

With His lotus-like hands, He holds a sword, a shield, a book, a jar of nectar, sacred grass and other items, a plow, a skull-topped staff, and a wish-fulfilling tree—He who is ten-armed and the destroyer of the pride of all enemies. (1)
Five-faced and most formidable, endowed with fifteen eyes and ten arms, he bestows the accomplishment of all desires and goals. (2)
In the east, however, is a monkey face, possessing a radiance equal to ten million suns, with a mouth formidable with fangs and eyes crooked with a frown.
But on the right side is another face, the most wonderful Nārasiṃha, blazing with exceedingly fierce splendor, terrifying yet the destroyer of fear. (4)
In the west is the face of Garuḍa, with a vajra beak and great strength; it pacifies all diseases and destroys poisons, malevolent spirits, and the like. (5)
In the north is the boar-faced [deity], with a sun as black and intensely radiant; he bestows success upon men in the netherworld and destroys fevers, diseases, and other ailments.
Above was his terrible horse-headed face, the supreme destroyer of the Dānavas, from which mouth, O best of Brahmins, all branches of knowledge issued forth.
As he meditates upon this five-faced one, it is not terrifying; [he holds] a sword, a trident, a khaṭvāṅga, an axe, a goad, and a mountain.
We worship Him who bears these various weapons: the pestle, the book, the nectar, the pitcher, and likewise the plough. (9)
Seated upon a preta-throne, adorned with divine ornaments, wearing divine garlands and garments, and anointed with divine perfumes.
Oṃ! O Lord of Monkeys, possessed of great energy, destroyer of all sorrow! Destroy my enemies, protect me, and grant me prosperity, O Lord! (11)
One should thus meditate upon the infinite God, whose faces are everywhere, who consists of all sovereignty, who has five faces, and who bestows the fruits of all desires. 12.
The five-faced, infallible one of manifold and diverse prowess, whose forearms are made beautiful by the auspicious conch and discus.
I meditate in my heart upon the noble monkey, resplendent with yellow garments, a crown, earrings, and anklets. 13.

I worship this son of Vidyā, who has a crescent moon upon his excellent pair of lotus-feet, who wears a loincloth and a girdle of muñja grass, whose garment is tied at the navel with a Vaiṣṇava thread, and who possesses an auspicious sacred thread; who holds his hands in the añjali gesture, who bears a string of pearls, earrings, and a lock of hair on his crown, and whose face is serene.
Oṃ! O Lord of Monkeys, of great energy, destroyer of all sorrow! Destroy my enemies, protect me, and grant me prosperity, O Lord! (15)
Thus ends the section on meditative concentration.
Now follows the mantra for the ritual application.
Oṃ, to Hari-markaṭa, the Great Monkey! Oṃ vaṃ vaṃ vaṃ vaṃ vaṃ vaṃ vauṣaṭ huṃ phaṭ ghe ghe ghe svāhā! (O you with the monkey-face!)
Oṃ, to Hari, the monkey, the great monkey; oṃ phaṃ phaṃ phaṃ phaṃ phaṃ phaṃ hūṃ phaṭ ghe ghe ghe svāhā (O you with the face of Narasiṃha)!
Oṃ, to Hari, the monkey, the great monkey! Oṃ kheṃ kheṃ kheṃ kheṃ kheṃ kheṃ hūṃ phaṭ ghe ghe ghe svāhā (in the face of Garuḍa).
Oṃ, to Hari, the monkey, the great monkey! Oṃ ṭhaṃ ṭhaṃ ṭhaṃ ṭhaṃ ṭhaṃ ṭhaṃ hūṃ phaṭ ghe ghe ghe! For the purpose of paralyzing, svāhā! (O you with the face of a boar!)
Oṃ, to Hari, the monkey, the great monkey! Oṃ oṃ oṃ oṃ oṃ oṃ oṃ hūṃ phaṭ ghe ghe ghe! To the seven who summon [beings], svāhā! (To Hayamukha!)

Oṃ Hari Markaṭa! This great mantra is inscribed, it is being inscribed upon the surface of the earth. If [the enemy] perishes, he perishes; if [the fetter] is released from the left hand, the chain is released. Thus is the mantra for the ritual application.
Oṃ. Now, the root mantra.
Oṃ, to Harimarkaṭa, the Great Monkey, hūṃ phaṭ ghe ghe ghe svāhā!

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One with five faces, whose eastern face is that of a monkey; Oṃ, to the glorious heroic Hanumān; Oṃ ṭhaṃ ṭhaṃ ṭhaṃ ṭhaṃ ṭhaṃ, for the destruction of all enemies, for the total eradication of every foe, to the one of great power! Huṃ phaṭ ghe ghe ghe ghe ghe ghe ghe svāhā! ||1||

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One with five faces, whose right face is the terrifying one, the glorious lion-faced one; Oṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ haṃ, to the subduer of all *bhūtas* and *pretas*, the remover of the great darkness of the sin of killing a Brahmin, the one of great power—huṃ phaṭ! ghe ghe ghe ghe ghe ghe ghe svāhā! ||2||

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One with five faces, who has the face of a heroic Garuḍa in the west; Oṃ, to the illustrious Vīra Hanumān! Oṃ maṃ maṃ maṃ maṃ maṃ maṃ, to Mahārudra, for the warding off of all diseases and poisons: huṃ phaṭ ghe ghe ghe ghe ghe ghe ghe svāhā! ||3||

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One who has five faces, whose foremost face is that of a boar; Oṃ, to the illustrious Vīra Hanumān! Oṃ, *laṃ* *laṃ* *laṃ* *laṃ* *laṃ* *laṃ*, to the giver of life to Lakṣmaṇa, to the burner of the city of Laṅkā, to the performer of all prosperity, to the one who brings about the increase of sons, grandsons, and so forth—*huṃ phaṭ ghe ghe ghe ghe ghe ghe svāhā*. ||4||

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One with five faces, whose face toward the upward direction is that of Hayagrīva; Oṃ, to the glorious Vīra Hanumān; Oṃ, *rūm̐* *rūm̐* *rūm̐* *rūm̐* *rūm̐* *rūm̐*, to the embodiment of Rudra, for the subjugation of all worlds, whose nature is the knowledge of the Vedas; *huṃ phaṭ*! *ghē ghē ghē ghē ghē ghē ghē*! Svāhā! ||5||
Thus ends the root mantra.
The Armor of Hanuman (Hanumat-kavaca)
Now begins the Kavaca (The Armor).

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, to Āñjaneya of great power, huṃ phaṭ! Ghe ghe ghe ghe ghe ghe ghe svāhā! Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, to the heroic Śrī Hanumān, possessed of manifest prowess, who has traversed the entire circle of the quarters; whose face is radiant; whose adamantine body is made white; who is meditated upon by the world; who is an incarnation of Rudra; who burned the city of Laṅkā; who leaped across the ocean; who bound the bridge; who trampled upon the heads of the ten-necked Rāvaṇa; and who comforted Sītā.

To the leader of infinite millions of universes; to the one of great strength; to the son of the Wind-god; to the one born from the womb of the goddess Añjanī; to the one who brings joy to Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa; to the one who acts for the pleasure of the monkey army; to the one who provides assistance to Sugrīva and accomplishes his tasks; to the one who uproots mountains; to the youthful celibate student; to the one from whom a deep sound arises: Oṃ rhīṃ klīṃ, for the warding off of all evil planets; for the eradication of all diseases and fevers;
for the destruction of Ḍākinīs and Śākinīs: Oṃ śrīṃ rhīṃ huṃ phaṭ ghe ghe ghe svāhā! ||6||

Oṃ, salutations to the Blessed One, the glorious Vīra Hanumān of great strength! For the warding off of all defects; for the eradication of all evil planets, diseases, and curses; for the eradication of all evil circles, including the circles of all spirits (*bhūta*), the circles of ghosts (*preta*), the circles of all *piśācas*, and so forth. Oṃ r̥hīṃ r̥haiṃ huṃ phaṭ ghe ghe ghe svāhā. ||7||

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the glorious Vīra Hanumān! Cut, cut all fevers of living beings; cut, cut all fevers of *pretas*—the quotidian, the tertian, the quartan, the burning, the irregular, the hidden, the fever of heat, the fever of cold, the fever of Maheśvarī, the fever of Vaiṣṇavī, and all fevers! Shatter, shatter the *yakṣas*, *rākṣasas*, and *brahmarākṣasas*! Expel, expel the *bhūtas*, *vetālas*, *pretas*, and *piśācas*! Oṃ r̥hāṃ r̥hīṃ r̥haiṃ huṃ phaṭ ghe ghe ghe svāhā! ||8||

Oṃ, salutation to the Blessed One, the glorious Vīra Hanumān. Oṃ rhāṃ rhīṃ rhaṃ rhaiṃ rhauṃ rhaḥ. Āha āha asatī asatī ehi ehi oṃ oṃ hoṃ hoṃ huṃ huṃ phaṭ ghe ghe ghe svāhā. Oṃ, salutation to the Blessed One, the glorious Vīra Hanumān, the son of the Wind; for the purpose of deluding the ḍākinīs and śākinīs and for their total eradication, render snake venom poisonless, render it poisonless! Drive them away, drive them away! Huṃ phaṭ ghe ghe ghe svāhā. 9.

Oṃ, salutation to the Blessed One, the illustrious Vīra Hanumān! For the purpose of dispelling the afflictions of lions, śarabhas, tigers, gaṇḍas, bheruṇḍas, and wild beasts, perform an assault! Perform an assault for the purpose of dispelling them! Ward off, ward off all diseases! Cry out, cry out! Crush, crush the enemies! Cut asunder, cut asunder the fear of madness! Shatter, shatter it!
Cut! Cut! Kill! Kill! Wither! Wither! Delude! Delude! Inflame! Inflame! Strike! Strike! Cut away, cut away all diseases! Oṃ r̥hīṃ r̥hūṃ huṃ phaṭ ghe ghe ghe svāhā! ||10||

Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Glorious Vīra Hanumān! Expel, expel all diseases and malevolent planets; agitate, agitate the enemy forces! Accomplish, accomplish all my tasks! Release, release from the shackles and bonds! Liberate, liberate me from prisons and the like! ||11||
Avert, avert the great diseases such as headache, earache, eyeache, abdominal pain, and side-pain! Destroy, destroy the entire host of enemies! 12.

Uproot the serpent-noose, uproot it! Oṃ! Ananta, Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Karkoṭaka, Kālagulika, Padma, Mahāpadma, Kumuda, Jalacara, Rātriñcara, Divācara, and so forth—render all poison poisonless, render it poisonless! 13.
Ward off all diseases, ward them off! Paralyze the mouths of all royal assemblies, paralyze them! Pacify all fear of kings, fear of thieves, and fear of fire, pacify them! ||14||

Cut, cut! Destroy, destroy! All foreign machines, supreme mantras, dependent spells, and the manifestation of rival sciences—terrify them, terrify them! Make manifest, make manifest all my own sciences; nourish, nourish them! Pacify, pacify all misfortunes! Annihilate, annihilate all enemies! ||15||
Ward off, ward off all afflictions caused by diseases and *piśācas*! Accomplish, accomplish the unaccomplishable task! Oṃ r̥hāṃ r̥hīṃ r̥hūṃ r̥haiṃ r̥hauṃ r̥haḥ huṃ phaṭ ghe ghe ghe svāhā! ||16||

The man who, being self-restrained, daily recites this armor (*kavaca*)—reciting it once every day destroys all enemies; reciting it twice every day subjugates all enemies; he who recites it thrice every day brings about auspiciousness and all prosperity; reciting it four times every day wards off all diseases; reciting it five times every day increases one's sons and grandsons; and reciting it six times every day brings all the gods under one's control.

Reciting it seven times daily bestows all good fortune; reciting it eight times daily grants the fulfillment of desired objects and aims; reciting it nine times along with the group of seven brings all kingdoms under one's control; reciting it ten times along with the pair of sevens provides the vision and knowledge of the three periods of time. By reciting this mantra twenty-one times, one shall become a conqueror of the three worlds together with one’s own kin, [overcoming] all diseases and all obstacles.

Repel, repel all afflictions arising from contact with all spirits, *pretas*, *piśācas*, *brahmarākṣasas*, *vetālas*, the sin of killing a Brahmin (*brahmahatyā*), and so forth! *Huṃ phaṭ ghe ghe ghe svāhā!* By merely remembering this armor (*kavaca*), one shall obtain great fruit. Whoever recites it at the time of worship shall find it grants success in all undertakings. Thus ends the *Śrīsītārāma-manohara-pañcamukhī-śrīvīrahanumat-kavaca-stotra*, the secret of the Atharvaṇa within the *Rudrayāmala*, according to the *Śrīsudarśana-saṃhitā*. It is complete.
May this be offered unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
